name: Bodegas Ysios
key_features: An undulating aluminium roof over cedar-clad walls echoes the mountain ridge behind the winery.

name: Casa no Butantã (Paulo Mendes da Rocha House)
key_features: One raised concrete floor on just four pillars; closed end walls, long window bands to east and west.

name: Casa Ugalde
key_features: White walls fanned out across a hillside toward the sea, shaped around the views and existing trees.

name: City Hall and Central Library, The Hague
key_features: Two white slabs enclose a vast glass-roofed atrium crossed by bridges, nicknamed the Ice Palace.

name: De Kunstlinie
key_features: One flat glass-edged box packs theatre halls, studios and small courtyards side by side by the lake.

name: Diego Rivera and Frida Kahlo House-Studio
key_features: Two functionalist studio houses, red and blue, joined by a roof bridge, with sawtooth roof lights.

name: Hiroshima City Museum of Contemporary Art
key_features: Row of storehouse-like roofs; materials rise from stone to tile to aluminium round an empty circular plaza.

name: Maison à Bordeaux
key_features: Three stacked houses; a 3 x 3.5 m lift platform moves through all levels for the wheelchair-using owner.

name: Reggio Emilia AV Mediopadana station
key_features: Calatrava's high-speed station on the Milan-Bologna line, with two side platforms.

name: Tomb of Nader Shah
key_features: Rough granite mass under a sharp angular canopy, with bronze riders of the shah's army.

name: Brazilian Press Association Building (ABI)
key_features: Office block wrapped in fixed concrete sun-breakers, among the first brise-soleil facades ever built.

name: American Republic Insurance Company Headquarters
key_features: Insurance headquarters completed in 1965; listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 2015.

name: Anzeiger-Hochhaus
key_features: Dark clinker-brick tower with vertical piers, topped by a copper dome that once held a planetarium.

name: Brücke Museum
key_features: Low single-storey galleries grouped around an inner courtyard at the edge of the Grunewald forest.

name: Butte-aux-Cailles swimming pool
key_features: One of the oldest swimming pools in Paris, on place Paul-Verlaine in the 13th arrondissement, designed by Louis Bonnier.

name: Café Seerose
key_features: Thin hyperbolic concrete shells fold out like water-lily petals over a café on the Havel.

name: Campus Palmas Altas (Sevilla)
key_features: A group of seven buildings by Richard Rogers and Luis Vidal Arquitectos, once Abengoa's headquarters.

name: Casa de Vidro
key_features: Glass-walled living floor on slender pilotis over a forested slope, with a tree rising through a central void.

name: De Vonk
key_features: Symmetrical brick holiday house with Van Doesburg's coloured brick and tile patterns at door and hall.

name: Echigo-Matsunoyama Museum of Natural Science (Kyororo)
key_features: Natural science museum noted by The Architectural Review in 2004; a Tezuka Architects work of 2003.

name: Edificio Panamericano
key_features: Long apartment slab raised on V-shaped concrete pilotis, facing the river at Buceo.

name: Maersk Tower
key_features: Research tower on a low landscaped base, wrapped in copper shutters that move with the sun.

name: Nira House (Leek House)
key_features: Roof ridge planted with a row of leeks in pots; walls of rough-split timber and hand-finished plaster.

name: Toho Gakuen School of Music
key_features: Concrete lesson rooms spaced apart by small courtyard-like gaps, with glass corners that let views and sound through.

name: Wells Fargo Center
key_features: César Pelli's 774-foot Minneapolis tower, a modernised Art Deco design that echoes nearby towers.

name: Circular School, Agios Dimitrios
key_features: A three-storey disc of classrooms round a central core, its south half ringed by louvred eaves at every floor.

name: Aomori Museum of Art
key_features: White brick box hovers over trench galleries cut into the ground, like an excavation.

name: Astrup Fearnley Museum
key_features: Curved glass roof on laminated timber beams sweeps over gallery buildings by the fjord.

name: Bat Yam City Hall
key_features: An inverted stepped pyramid of concrete around an inner court, with a faceted polyhedral roof.

name: Casa Klotz
key_features: A white timber box, 6 x 6 x 12 m, nearly closed to the south and opened to the beach with a double-height living room.

name: Casa Rotalinti
key_features: A Brutalist house by Aurelio Galfetti in Bellinzona, built by 1961 and listed as regionally important.

name: Dialogue Centre Przełomy
key_features: History museum hidden under a city square whose paving rises into slopes; a hard-edged pavilion marks one corner.

name: Gobierno Civil de Tarragona
key_features: Competition-winning seat of government in natural stone; about half its area is housing, all furnished by De la Sota.

name: Lanaras Weekend House
key_features: Two thin concrete slabs on slender steel posts, glazed and shuttered between, above stone terrace walls.

name: Lyon Museum of Contemporary Art
key_features: Flexible galleries built behind the kept 1930s facade of the old exhibition hall in the Cité Internationale.

name: Nakagawa-machi Bato Hiroshige Museum
key_features: Local cedar louvres cover roof and walls alike, filtering light into galleries lined with washi paper.

name: Nantes Courthouse
key_features: A black grid of slender columns and a vast dark hall give a severe image of justice by the Loire.

name: Nilson Nelson Gymnasium
by: Cláudio Cianciarullo, Ícaro de Castro Mello, Eduardo de Castro Mello
key_features: Indoor arena opened in 1973; a 2008 renovation cut capacity from 24,286 to 11,105 seats.

name: Otaniemi Chapel
key_features: The wall behind the altar is fully glazed onto a forest holding a cross, under a timber truss roof.

name: 23 de Enero Superblocks
key_features: Fifteen-storey slab blocks with skip-floor corridors house thousands on the hills above downtown.

name: Accordia
by: Feilden Clegg Bradley Studios, Alison Brooks Architects, Maccreanor Lavington
key_features: Dense brick terraces, mews and courtyards set among mature trees; the first housing scheme to win the Stirling Prize.

name: Austin City Hall
key_features: Designed to reflect the city's vitality; built partly with recycled materials.

name: Bauhaus-Archiv
key_features: Shed roofs with curved north-light profiles crown a low white gallery block.

name: Beira railway station
by: Paulo de Melo Sampaio, Francisco Castro
key_features: Tropical modernist station: a long concrete concourse below a tower block, with shaded facades.

name: Benedictine Monastery Chapel
key_features: Two interlocked white masonry cubes, rotated against each other, lit by hidden slots of indirect light.

name: Cairo Opera House
key_features: A gift from Japan to Egypt, built 1985-88 to give Cairo a new opera house after the Khedivial Opera.

name: Camino Real Hotel, Mexico City
key_features: Magenta lattice wall screens a sequence of courtyards and pools from the street.

name: Casa delle Armi
key_features: Luigi Moretti's experimental Casa del Balilla, designed in 1934 and finished in 1936 as a fencing academy.

name: Casa Rozes
key_features: Coderch's 1961–62 clifftop house, stepped down in cube-like levels beneath a cantilevered terrace.

name: Central Library, Central University of Venezuela
key_features: Main library of the Central University of Venezuela, inaugurated 1953.

name: Chiesa del Santo Volto
key_features: Seven towers ring a central church; an old steelworks chimney becomes its bell tower.

name: Children's Memorial, Yad Vashem
key_features: An underground hollow where a few candles, reflected by mirrors, multiply into endless points of light.

name: Church of Saint Peter, Durazno
key_features: Reinforced-brick walls and a folded brick roof spanning the nave without columns.

name: de Young Museum
key_features: A perforated, dimpled copper skin wraps low galleries and a twisting tower in Golden Gate Park.

name: Diehtosiida
key_features: A Sámi academic campus in Kautokeino housing the Sámi University College, Sámi Archives and other institutions; opened 2009.

name: Dominican Chapel, Ibadan
key_features: Thick walls, a shaded ambulatory and carved timber details keep the chapel cool and dim.

name: Galleria Department Store (West)
key_features: A blind 1970s concrete box re-clad in 4,330 glass discs that shift colour by day and glow with LEDs by night.

name: Grande Poste d'Alger
key_features: Neo-Moorish central post office, Algeria's largest; arcaded facade; a museum since 2015.

name: Haus Freudenberg
key_features: Hermann Muthesius's Berlin-Nikolassee house for Hermann Freudenberg, now under monument protection.

name: Hospital Naval Pedro Mallo
key_features: Testa's sculptural concrete hospital on the edge of Parque Centenario, often read as a moored ship.

name: House of Wisdom
key_features: A thin floating roof overhangs the two-storey glass library by 15 m on every side, shading it from the desert sun.

name: MADRE Museum
key_features: Siza adapted the Palazzo Donnaregina over four floors; a roof terrace carries Paladino's sculpture Cavallo.

name: Mivtachim Sanitarium (ELMA Arts Complex and Hotel)
key_features: Brutalist retreat for workers, designed 1966 and completed 1969; later reopened as the ELMA hotel.

name: Deutsche Bank Place
key_features: Service core pushed to one side so column-free office floors open to harbour views.

name: Shiba Ryotaro Memorial Museum
key_features: A curved concrete and glass hall holds a towering wall of bookshelves beside the writer's house and garden.

name: Akino Fuku Art Museum
key_features: A hand-built hilltop museum of rough plastered walls, timber details and a small lookout tower.

name: Igrejinha Nossa Senhora de Fátima
key_features: A thin concrete roof shaped like a nun's hat rests on three points over a tiny chapel with tile murals.

name: Tour de Lille
key_features: An L-shaped office tower straddling Lille Europe station, nicknamed the ski boot.

name: Boston Public Library, McKim Building
key_features: Granite palazzo front of arched windows over the vaulted Bates Hall reading room and an arcaded courtyard.

name: Anacleto Angelini Innovation Center
key_features: A solid concrete block with deep-set openings and a hollow core, shielding the offices from sun and glare.

name: Atatürk Library
key_features: Concrete library with overhanging upper floors and screens, echoing Ottoman wooden houses.

name: Darat al Funun
key_features: Three 1920s houses and Byzantine ruins on a hillside converted into galleries, studios and gardens.

name: Dominion Tower
key_features: Stacked floor plates shift out over one another around a white skylit atrium of zigzag stairs.

name: Mikimoto Ginza 2
key_features: Pale pink walls of concrete poured between steel plates carry the floors; irregular windows are cut at random.

name: Museum of Sydney
key_features: Sandstone-walled museum built over the remains of the first Government House (1788), by a forecourt of poles.

name: 140 Broadway
key_features: A 51-storey International Style tower with a smooth black facade and Isamu Noguchi's Cube sculpture at its entrance.

name: New York State Cultural Education Center
key_features: Eleven-storey New Formalist building on Empire State Plaza housing the State Museum, Archives and Library.

name: Jyväskylä City Theatre
key_features: Municipal theatre founded in 1961; the current building dates from 1982.

name: Didrichsen Art Museum
key_features: A Helsinki art museum of 1965, designed by Viljo Revell.

name: De Doelen
key_features: Concert venue rebuilt in 1966 after the 1934 original was destroyed in 1940; a Rijksmonument since 2015.

name: Yaoko Kawagoe Museum
key_features: A Kawagoe art museum showing the works of Western-style painter Misu Yuji.

name: Gallery of Modern Art
key_features: Thin flat roof floating over glazed galleries and a deep shaded verandah facing the river.

name: Church of Saint-Nicolas, Hérémence
key_features: A craggy cluster of rough concrete volumes rises like a rock outcrop above the mountain village.

name: Scharoun Theatre Wolfsburg
key_features: Fan-shaped auditorium and flowing, asymmetric foyer levels in Scharoun's organic plan.

name: Civic Center of Lima
key_features: A tall exposed-concrete tower and lower blocks set around raised plazas and terraces in central Lima.

name: Jeevan Bharati Building
key_features: Two red sandstone and glass blocks linked by a giant pergola that frames a plaza on Connaught Place.

name: Santa Maria Immacolata, Longarone
key_features: Rebuilt after the 1963 Vajont flood: a concrete church whose roof is a curved open-air amphitheatre.

name: Amorepacific Headquarters
key_features: A near-cube wrapped in vertical sun screens, with large openings cut into three faces as raised gardens.

name: The Opus
key_features: A glass cube with a free-form void carved through its middle, splitting it into two towers joined above and below.

name: Baku Crystal Hall
by: gmp Architekten (von Gerkan, Marg and Partners)
key_features: Arena on the Caspian shore wrapped in a faceted membrane skin that lights up at night.

name: Study Pavilion, TU Braunschweig
key_features: A light steel frame of open, fully glazed study floors with outside stairs, built to be taken apart.

name: Shiroiya Hotel
key_features: A renovated 1970s hotel paired with a new Green Tower: a grassy mound planted with shrubs and trees.

name: Tautra Mariakloster (convent)
key_features: Cistercian convent on a fjord island: slate-clad walls and lattice glass-and-timber roofs, near medieval ruins.

name: Biosphere (Bigo)
key_features: Glass-and-steel sphere 20 m across weighing 60 tonnes, with movable sails that shade it from the sun.

name: Central Bank of Ireland, Dame Street
key_features: Ireland's only suspended structure building, eight floors hanging from central concrete cores.

name: Bergen Kunsthall
key_features: Early functionalist art hall designed in 1935.

name: Church of the Holy Spirit, Wolfsburg
key_features: Lutheran church and parish centre; design completed and building started in 1961.

name: Aschanska Villa
key_features: A listed Umeå villa by Ragnar Östberg, completed in 1906 for a colonel and now a restaurant.

name: Campus Einaudi
key_features: A Turin university campus on Lungo Dora Siena, named after Italy's second president, Luigi Einaudi.

name: 66 Old Church Street, Chelsea
key_features: Gropius and Fry's house for the politician and playwright Benn Levy, part of a joint scheme with Cohen House.

name: Alfa Palace
key_features: A functionalist building by Bohuslav Fuchs, with an inner arcade linking two streets and a square.

name: Dortmund City and State Library
key_features: Mario Botta's central library, opposite Dortmund's main station; moved in May 1999.

name: Cine Brasília
key_features: Oscar Niemeyer's cinema in Brasília, opened on 22 April 1960 during the new capital's inauguration.

name: Vestersøhus
key_features: A seven-storey red-brick block by Kay Fisker and C. F. Møller, a key work of Danish functionalism, completed 1939.

name: Adria Palace
key_features: A cubist monument in Prague's New Town, facing the ARA palace.

name: Casa Cattaneo
key_features: Cesare Cattaneo's best-known rationalist building, a 1938–39 rental house in Cernobbio, designed without client constraints.

name: Secretariat Building
key_features: Long concrete slab with a brise-soleil grid, a roof terrace and sculptural ramp towers.

name: Church on the Water
key_features: A glass wall slides fully open onto a shallow pool holding a steel cross against the forest.

name: Wohnpark Alt-Erlaa
key_features: Stepped slabs with planted terraces on the lower floors and rooftop swimming pools for all residents.

name: Matthäuskirche Pforzheim
key_features: Walls of a concrete honeycomb grid infilled with coloured glass blocks fill the church with tinted light.

name: Co-Cathedral of the Great Mother of God (Gran Madre di Dio)
key_features: A pierced, sail-like white screen rises above the church and is reflected in pools below.

name: Agora Theatre
key_features: A faceted, folded skin of orange and yellow panels wraps the stage tower and foyers.

name: Diözesanmuseum Paderborn
key_features: Lead-clad block beside the cathedral, holding one tall hall of stepped gallery platforms.

name: ECLAC Building
key_features: Raised square ring of concrete offices around a courtyard, beside a spiral ramp and a conical council chamber.

name: House in Cap Ferret
key_features: Raised on twelve micro-piles among the pines; the trees pass straight through the house in flexible sleeves.

name: Dornbusch Church
key_features: 1960s church partly torn down and closed by a new wall keeping imprints of the old; its footprint is marked outside.

name: Alila Villas Uluwatu
key_features: Clifftop resort of low terraced villas and open lattice pavilions, built with local stone and reclaimed timber.

name: Shoto Museum of Art
key_features: Curved wall of rough Korean granite under a bronze-louvred eave; galleries round a deep light well with fountains.

name: Leeza SOHO
key_features: Glass tower split by a 194 m atrium that twists 45 degrees up its height, the world's tallest.

name: University of Deusto Library
key_features: Compact library block with chamfered corners, wrapped in glass behind a fine metal screen.

name: Basílica del Salvador
key_features: Neo-Gothic brick basilica, designed by Teodoro Burchard and completed in 1932; damaged in 1985 and 2010.

name: Durban City Hall
key_features: Edwardian neo-baroque city hall, almost an exact replica of Belfast City Hall; built 1906-1910.

name: Stephanuskirche (Wolfsburg)
key_features: A church and parish center by Alvar Aalto, a prominent example of International modernism in Germany.

name: 1101 New York Avenue
key_features: A Washington office tower whose corners are notched to give more window offices.

name: Huis Hillebrand
key_features: Rietveld's 1934–1935 house in The Hague, with a low tent roof that looks flat from close up.

name: Dům obuvi Baťa (Liberec)
key_features: A functionalist high-rise shoe store in Liberec from 1932, a cultural monument since 1987.

name: Ullsteinhaus
key_features: A brick expressionist landmark in Berlin-Tempelhof, 77 m tall, and for 30 years Germany's tallest high-rise.

name: Brno Crematorium
key_features: Arnošt Wiesner's crematorium at Brno Central Cemetery, built to his plans in 1926–1929 on Jihlavská Street.

name: Shanghai Symphony Hall
key_features: Isozaki and Toyota's concert hall in Shanghai, home of the Shanghai Symphony Orchestra, opened 6 September 2014.

name: Dorfkirche Kunersdorf
key_features: A late-Expressionist brick village church in Brandenburg, listed as a monument, by Curt Steinberg.
